chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from al-Fudayl, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
“When a free man confesses against himself to theft once before the Imam, his hand is cut off.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Confession to theft requires two times; as for one time, it does not make cutting off obligatory. We have already mentioned that earlier. The proper way regarding this narration is that we carry it upon a form of taqiyyah, because it accords with the views of some of the generality. As for the narrations we presented earlier stating that when he confesses he is cut off, there is nothing in them specifying whether it is once or twice; rather, they are general. Since the hadiths we presented are detailed, acting upon them is appropriate, and what he narrated further increases this in clarification:

key_terms.قُطِعَ: his hand is cut off, meaning the hadd punishment is carried out
key_terms.مُجْمَلَةٌ: general or unspecified, lacking detail about the number of confessions
key_terms.ٱلتَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity due to prevailing circumstances
key_terms.ٱلْإِقْرَارُ: formal confession or admission of guilt
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the Imam, before whom the confession is made in this legal context
key_terms.ٱلْحُرُّ: a free person, as distinct from a slave, in the legal ruling
key_terms.ٱلْقَطْعَ: amputation, the legal hadd penalty for theft

ai.seo_question: How many times must theft be confessed before the Imam for the hadd punishment to be carried out in Shi'i hadith?
ai.summary: This report states that a free person who confesses to theft once before the Imam is subject to amputation, but Shaykh al-Tusi explains that the established ruling requires two confessions. He reconciles the report by treating it as taqiyyah and gives preference to the more detailed narrations on the issue.
